question: Why does Arjuna say Krishna's form has no end, middle, or beginning?
premises: Arjuna sees many arms, bellies, faces, and eyes
The form is endless on every side
He sees no end, middle, or beginning
inference: Arjuna declares Krishna's universal form boundless and without limits.
uncertainties: Fused sandhi forms analyzed as wholes
plain_english: I see you with many arms, bellies, faces, and eyes, endless in form on every side; I see no end, no middle, and no beginning again, O lord of the universe, universal form!
